title: Columbia STS-107: foam-strike warning, imagery requests, and proof-burden inversion
summary: CAIB Volume I is promoted here not merely as a foam-strike record but as a warning-governance record: the Board gave physical and organizational causes, documented that debris assessment uncertainty did not land with sufficient management force, and explicitly found that engineers had to prove unsafety rather than the program having to prove safety.

status_history.note: Seed listed Columbia as a spaceflight failure but no prior queue row existed; promoted directly with CAIB Volume I.

place.event_context: Launch from Kennedy Space Center; re-entry loss over the United States; mission management and debris assessment primarily in NASA program channels

claims.claim: The CAIB identified Columbia’s physical cause as a breach in the Thermal Protection System on the leading edge of the left wing caused by insulating foam from the External Tank striking the wing during launch.
what_would_change_status: A later official source materially revises the physical-cause statement.

claims.claim: The CAIB intentionally weighted organizational causes alongside physical cause, finding that management practices, NASA history/culture, resource constraints, fluctuating priorities, and schedule pressures contributed to the accident.

type_payload.system: Space Shuttle Orbiter/external tank foam/Thermal Protection System plus mission-management decision process

sequence_of_events.event: Foam separated from the External Tank during launch and struck the left wing.
Debris assessment formed but uncertainty, imagery requests, and potential RCC damage analysis did not land as decisive safety-of-flight action.
Management discussions focused partly on turnaround/schedule implications and required evidence of unsafety.
During re-entry, superheated air entered through the Thermal Protection System breach, causing structural failure and loss of vehicle and crew.

type_payload.proximate_cause: Foam-strike-induced breach in left-wing Thermal Protection System leading to re-entry structural failure.
type_payload.proof_burden_observation: CAIB makes the proof-burden inversion explicit: engineers had to produce evidence that the system was unsafe rather than program managers requiring proof it was safe.
contributing_factors: schedule context around downstream Shuttle/Station milestones
latent_conditions: Foam loss migrated from anomaly/hazard to in-family/maintenance category.
Post-Challenger safety reforms did not prevent later warning-routing and culture failures.
Resource and schedule contexts altered how uncertainty was interpreted.
decisions_that_mattered: Not obtaining decisive imagery or treating uncertainty as requiring action.
Treating absence of proof of danger as sufficient for no action.
Allowing unresolved STS-112 foam history and STS-107 strike to remain below a binding no-flight/no-entry safety threshold.
type_payload.record_grain_warning: This is a CAIB Volume I extraction; subsequent volumes and NASA corrective-action records remain to be added.

handling_notes: Seven crew members died; avoid sensationalism and avoid freezing their deaths as a management aphorism.
Do not reproduce family or crew details beyond what is necessary for event identity.
Future public surface should include a dignity review before images/video are displayed.
